LLM_description:
Situation:
Joint Task Force logistics are supporting dispersed ground elements operating from Forward Operating Base Alpha and Battalion Iron. Multiple supply depots across the theater hold critical stocks. Ground movement corridors include exposed valley routes under observation and intermittent indirect fire, mountain passes with limited width and degraded road surfaces, and river crossings subject to washouts. Enemy IED activity and complex ambushes require convoy escort, route clearance teams, and movement control oversight. Weather, route condition, and security restrictions compress movement windows and limit feasible convoy schedules.

Mission:
Deliver required sustainment to the supported elements while minimizing total operational cost. Costs include transport along selected routes, shortage penalties for unmet demand, vehicle deployment expenses, and fixed route security risk costs associated with activating any movement corridor. Maintain readiness by meeting demand where feasible, while controlling exposure and resource expenditure.

Execution/Concept:
- Distribution will be time-phased by day and planned at the depot-to-unit level per supply type. Shipments from any depot will not exceed that depot’s available supply for the period. Each unit’s demand is to be met by inbound flows; any shortfall is tracked as slack and penalized accordingly.
- Convoys are constrained by vehicle capacity. The deliverable volume per route and day must not exceed the product of vehicle capacity and the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.
- Vehicles can only move on routes that are explicitly activated for that depot-to-unit pairing and day. Activating a route (sending any vehicles) incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing route clearance, escort detachments, overwatch, and movement control. This fixed Risk Cost applies regardless of the number of vehicles subsequently sent on that activated route.
- Fleet size is limited; total vehicles dispatched across all routes and depots per day cannot exceed the available fleet. Consolidation of loads onto fewer activated routes is preferred where feasible to amortize the fixed route security overhead.
- Priority of effort is to employ lower-risk, lower-transport-cost corridors where terrain and security permit, and to activate only those routes where shipment volumes justify the fixed Risk Cost. If demand cannot be fully met without disproportionate risk or cost, accept controlled shortages with associated penalties while preserving critical combat power.
- Movement control will coordinate departure windows, security tasking, and clearance sequencing. Convoy timing will avoid predictable patterns, deconflict with maneuver elements, and adapt to route condition changes. Alternate routing is prepared if primary corridors are denied or degraded.
